clue.text: Tedious attire is nothing to me

parts.note: attire is what you wear, so the noun gives WEAR
taken as written
nothing is zero, the letter O
the pronoun me, taken as written with the link 'to'

explanation.surface: Someone finds dressing up a chore that means nothing to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attire' reads as a noun but supplies the verb sense wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wearisome is dull and tiring, which is exactly what tedious describes.

clue.text: Perturbed sandpiper given guidance

parts.note: the ruff is a wading bird of the sandpiper family
to be given guidance is to be led

explanation.surface: A wading bird is upset while being shepherded along.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruffled feelings are disturbed or agitated ones, a common synonym of perturbed.

clue.text: Means to become a light house engineer

indicators.note: the letters are told to turn into something else, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as part of the fodder

explanation.surface: An instruction on how to qualify as a lighthouse builder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to become' tells you MEANS plus TO is to be rearranged. John Smeaton built the third Eddystone Lighthouse off Plymouth in the 1750s; 'light house' split in two hides the fact that it is one building.
explanation.definitionFit: John Smeaton, the eighteenth-century civil engineer, designed the famous Eddystone lighthouse.

clue.text: Amin's address in the South of France?

parts.note: M is short for Monsieur, the French form of address for a man
Idi was the first name of the Ugandan dictator Amin

explanation.surface: Where would a deposed dictator live on the Riviera?
explanation.walkthrough: Addressing Amin in French would be 'M. Idi', and the Midi is the name for the south of France.
explanation.definitionFit: The Midi is the French name for the southern region of the country.

clue.text: Racing motorist who very quickly takes over?

definitions.text: Racing motorist who very quickly takes over?

parts.words: Racing motorist who very quickly takes over?
parts.note: a slangy term for a fast driver, read as a trader who seizes companies at high speed

explanation.surface: A dealer who completes takeovers at a gallop, or a fast driver.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second picture: a businessman whose deals happen at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for anyone who drives or runs very fast, especially a racing driver.

clue.text: Win recognition as a fighting director

definitions.text: Win recognition as a fighting director

parts.words: Win recognition as a fighting director
parts.note: to be recognised as the leader of a military force is to take charge of it

explanation.surface: Becoming known as the person who directs a battle.
explanation.definitionFit: To take charge of troops is to become their acknowledged leader in combat.

clue.text: Just what the doctor ordered

parts.note: the idiom for something ideal, read literally as a prescribed quantity of medicine

explanation.surface: The familiar phrase for exactly the thing needed.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means 'ideal'; taken literally it describes the exact amount a doctor prescribes.
explanation.definitionFit: A prescription states the exact measured amount of medicine the physician wants taken.

clue.text: Literarily unromantic

parts.note: in literary history the ... style is set against the Romantic movement

explanation.surface: A description of writing that lacks passion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unromantic' looks like 'lacking love', but it means not belonging to the Romantic movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Classical literature favours order and restraint, the opposite pole to Romanticism.

clue.text: Dry leaves changed for the worse

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are altered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as fodder
taken as written as fodder

explanation.surface: Dried-up foliage has deteriorated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' looks like part of the sentence about the leaves but tells you to rearrange DRY LEAVES.
explanation.definitionFit: Something affected adversely has been harmed, that is, changed in a negative direction.

clue.text: I was first out, but concealed the fact

indicators.note: the letter that stood at the front is moved out of that place to a later spot

parts.note: the letter I
someone who was first led the field

explanation.surface: A runner admits leading but then hiding the truth.
explanation.walkthrough: I plus LED makes ILED; the I that 'was first' is moved out of the front, giving L-I-ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie is to tell an untruth, hiding what really happened.

clue.text: Members of which are much seen in church

definitions.text: Members of which are much seen in church

parts.words: Members of which are much seen in church
parts.note: the word for the clergy as a body, whose members are naturally in church a lot

explanation.surface: A group whose members are regular churchgoers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The cloth' is an old expression for the clergy; the surface also hints at fabric used for vestments.
explanation.definitionFit: 'The cloth' is a traditional collective term for priests and ministers.

clue.text: An irrational way to back us initially

indicators.note: the turned word comes at the start, before the road
the word us is turned to run backwards

parts.note: taken as written before turning
Rd is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A muddled route that leads us backwards first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns US into SU; 'initially' puts SU at the front, then RD follows.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a surd is an irrational root, such as the square root of two, so 'an irrational' is a noun here.

clue.text: Airy-fairy?

parts.note: the phrase usually means vague, but read literally it describes a spirit of the air

explanation.surface: A dismissive word for something vague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Airy-fairy' normally means fanciful; split up it describes an elemental spirit of the air.
explanation.definitionFit: A sylph is a slender air spirit of folklore, a fairy creature of the air.

clue.text: The stuff he left out of the will

indicators.note: he is removed from the words that follow

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man was disinherited of some possessions in a testament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out of the will' suggests disinheritance, but it removes HE from THE WILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Twill is a woven fabric, and stuff is an old word for cloth.

clue.text: Some day it could be one of the big attractions at Cruft's

definitions.text: one of the big attractions at Cruft's

indicators.note: the letters might, rearranged, form something else

parts.note: taken as written as fodder

explanation.surface: A hopeful forecast about winning at a famous show.
explanation.walkthrough: Crufts is a major British dog show held each year; 'it could be' signals rearranging SOME DAY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Samoyed is a fluffy white dog breed regularly shown at the big dog show.

clue.text: Quite out of place in Britain today?

parts.note: today means now
for a British newspaper reader, Britain is here

explanation.surface: A complaint that something no longer fits in modern Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as NOW HERE: 'today' and 'in Britain' as seen by a British reader.
explanation.definitionFit: Nowhere means in no place at all, completely absent.

clue.text: Breaks in a new stirrup

indicators.note: the word is given a new form, so its letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written as fodder

explanation.surface: A rider breaks in a fresh stirrup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaks in' looks like breaking in a horse or new tack, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrupt is to burst in forcibly, to enter suddenly.

clue.text: Shakespearian justice observed in a Trappist monastery

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean magistrate visits silent monks.
explanation.walkthrough: Justice Silence is a country justice in Shakespeare's Henry IV Part 2.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustic magistrate in Henry IV Part 2 bears this name; Trappist monks keep a rule of not speaking.

clue.text: Ring us about nothing? How cruel!

indicators.note: the words put around the zero letter

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them
taken as written
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone never phones, which seems heartless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts CALL US round O. 'How cruel!' is an exclamation standing for the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A callous person is unfeeling and heartless towards others.

clue.text: A hundred Mediterranean islanders holding a dance in Hungary

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: the islanders wrap around the single letter

parts.note: Sards are people of Sardinia

explanation.surface: Many Sardinians perform a Hungarian folk dance together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' places A inside SARDS. The csardas is spelt this way as well as czardas.
explanation.definitionFit: The csardas is a traditional Hungarian folk dance with slow and fast sections.

clue.text: Bill and he require the. attentions masseur, possibly

taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: The copy as held drops 'of a': the definition reads 'require the attentions of a masseur, possibly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sore muscles that throb with pain call for a massage.

clue.text: Quietly go ahead and address the court

parts.note: p is the musical notation for piano, quietly

explanation.surface: Advice to a barrister to speak softly before the judge.
explanation.definitionFit: To plead is to make a case formally before a judge.

explanation.surface: Fruit is offered to a young German.
explanation.definitionFit: Emil is a common German boy's given name.

clue.text: Clique of about fifty can

indicators.note: the tin is placed around the Roman numeral

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A group of about fifty people can form a clique.
explanation.definitionFit: A clan, like a clique, is a close group of people bound together.

clue.text: A plain black key

explanation.surface: A plain black piano key.
explanation.walkthrough: A flat is a stretch of level ground; on a piano the black keys sound flats (or sharps).
explanation.definitionFit: Level open ground is called a flat; a black piano key gives a note lowered by a semitone.

clue.text: A tree that doesn't grow straight up a ramp?

definitions.text: A tree that doesn't grow straight up

explanation.surface: A leaning tree climbs a slope.
explanation.walkthrough: The plane is a tree; one leaning over is 'inclined'. The two halves read as one sentence.
